articles.title: Causticline
articles.summary: Dark teal near-chrome with bright aqua light-caustic veins rippling across it, like sunlit pool water on metal. Reads as a dark teal-green metal with faint lighter aqua veins, moody and watery; the veins blur into a marbled shimmer.
articles.what: Refracted-ray bunching — a pool-light caustic network in aqua. Assign as a BASE; FRACTURED FORGE math-engine finish — near-chrome body that ignites at grazing angles. Up close: Dark teal ground with a web of thin glowing aqua threads that wander, branch and tangle like the bright net of light at the bottom of a pool. Lines are 3 to 6 px wide, soft-edged, joining into brighter knots; large dark pools between them. Not a loud picture. From a distance: Reads as a dark teal-green metal with faint lighter aqua veins, moody and watery; the veins blur into a marbled shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 247, roughness 45, coat 254. Shine: gloss. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, hood.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Causticline" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: near-chrome with veins looks best across big surfaces
Hood and roof for the reflection plus veins
Dark and calm with thin lines: white, aqua or yellow numbers read well; dark teal and black numbers disappear.
Thin white or aqua stripes: clean lines over the web
Pairs well with: white, chrome, silver, black.
pitfalls: Not bright aqua: the base colour is a dark teal
Not marble: the veins glow and are thin, no solid colour patches
Avoid: small numbers over the busy veins, next to other chrome finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 247 (chrome or mirror tier), roughness 45 (high gloss), clearcoat 254 (almost no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the busy veins, next to other chrome finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: thin white or aqua stripes: clean lines over the web; bold dark graphics: little contrast on the dark ground, so go big
Patterns to avoid: other chrome or glitter patterns: duplicate the reflective feel; fine texture overlays: bury the veins
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat, already high; a light sparkle for more pool shimmer
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Cellwave
articles.summary: Emerald-teal cracked cells with soft wave rings, glossy full-metal surface, low sparkle and gentle contrast. Reads as a sea-green metallic with a bold cobbled pattern of rippled tiles; the seams stay visible and the ripples read as light and dark patches.
articles.what: Voronoi cells modulated by radial wave interference — emerald cells pulsing under moire. FRACTURED FORGE finish. Up close: Large irregular cells, like a giraffe or dried-lakebed net, divided by thin dark seams. Inside each cell, soft concentric ripples swirl around an off-centre point, shading from dark green through bright mint. Cells are about 50-100 px across; edges crisp, insides smooth. From a distance: Reads as a sea-green metallic with a bold cobbled pattern of rippled tiles; the seams stay visible and the ripples read as light and dark patches. Measured spec (average): metal 241, roughness 64, coat 252. Shine: satin. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.

Tough: busy cells and ripples cut across numbers, so use a solid white or black plate with a border.
Thin outlines or pinstripes: sit cleanly across the cell seams

pitfalls: Not scales or fish skin: cells are irregular with no overlap
Not a flat metallic green: strong dark and light ripples inside every cell
Avoid: numbers over the cells, next to another patterned finish.

articles.title: Conduit
articles.summary: Pale ice-blue diamond lattice of dark dots on satin metal, crisp repeating geometric grid. Reads as an icy pale-blue car with a regular dark-dot grid, like perforated aluminium or a tech facade; the dots survive at distance.
articles.what: An isometric strut lattice warped into flowing steel conduits. Assign as a BASE; FRACTURED FORGE math-engine finish. Up close: A perfectly regular tiling of hexagon cells about 55 px apart. Each has a pale ice-blue glowing ring and a soft black six-pointed hole in the centre, with steel-blue struts and small three-way joints at the corners. Smooth shaded bevels, no grain. From a distance: Reads as an icy pale-blue car with a regular dark-dot grid, like perforated aluminium or a tech facade; the dots survive at distance. Measured spec (average): metal 237, roughness 75, coat 251. Shine: satin. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.

Not carbon fibre or woven: the surface is smooth bevelled metal

Spec overlays that work: none: spec is already uniform satin metal; a light brushed spec: adds a hint of grain to smooth struts

Brick-like subdivisions, every tile a flat solid colour with a faint inner shade at the edge. From a distance: A patchwork of earthy rust, teal and olive blocks outlined in pale gold; from a distance the mortar lines merge into a light grid and the blocks read as a muted mosaic.
